notes.body:
Fixed in `bf82f7c93`, with the first of your two fixes: the slot is kept out of reuse.

- **The mark is in one place for the failed purges.** `vessel_delete_persistence()` holds the slot from before its transaction until the purge commits, so every caller that frees the slot after a failed purge leaves it held: the three you list, and the spawn rollback (`src/vessels/vessels_edit.c`, "could not be persisted"), which ignored the result as well. Boot marks the slot at the two places you cite.
- **A spawn takes only a free slot.** `vedit_find_free_slot()` asks `vessel_slot_free()`: no hull in play or stowed, and no rows held.
- **Staff can see and clear it.** `shiplist` lists a held slot ("stored records of a hull that is not in the game; SHIPPURGE removes them") and counts it as in use. `shippurge <slot>` on one deletes the rows, the settlement with them, and frees the slot.
- **The mark is runtime only.** Every boot reads the rows again, so a later boot still loads her, which is the record's other exit.

The dock-fee restore is unchanged. With the slot held it reaches only the hull that paid the fee; the unowned stranger was the case. A hull whose owner is removed already keeps a fee she owes, so an unowned hull with a fee is not a state the restore adds.

**Tests.** Your probe is now `Test_vessel_settlement_holds_the_slot_of_a_hull_not_in_memory`, and the failed purge in it is made by the real code (the purge loses its connection at `DELETE FROM ship_interiors`):

- the rows and the settlement stay, the slot is not free, and Tern's login and `cargobuy` wait;
- `shiplist` shows the slot, and a `shippurge` that fails again leaves it held;
- the `shippurge` that commits removes the rows and the settlement, frees the slot, and his next `cargobuy` goes through.

**Live** (private-namespace harness, reload of the development dump): slot 13, the lowest free one, was given a `ship_interiors` row with no runtime snapshot and a settlement row. Boot logged "Dynamic ship 13 has no runtime snapshot; leaving it inactive and its slot held", and then:

```text
  13 (stored records of a hull that is not in the game; SHIPPURGE removes them)
> vedit spawn 3      Spawned 'Persistence_Tern' (Transport) as ship 14
> shippurge 13       Slot 13 held the stored records of a hull that is not in the game. They are removed and the slot is free.
> vedit spawn 3      Spawned 'Persistence_Tern' (Transport) as ship 13
```

No settlement and no `ship_interiors` row were left for the slot.

The help entry SHIP-ADMIN and `docs/systems/VESSEL_SYSTEM.md` (Two-phase settlements, Persistence Lifecycle) describe held slots.

**[P3] The row is deleted on a save that a host crash can still lose**

**Location.** `vessel_settlement_pay()` deletes the row as soon as `save_char_checked()` returns TRUE (this line). `save_char_checked()` (`src/player/players.c:4136-4153`) fsyncs the temporary file and renames it over the live one, and never fsyncs the directory. The rename is then durable only at the filesystem's next journal commit (ext4: up to 5 seconds by default), while the `DELETE` is durable at once (InnoDB flushes its log at commit by default).

**Repro.** Power loss, or a crash of the host or VM, inside that window after a trade. On restart the directory still names the old file (old gold, old `VSet`), the ship's side is committed, and no row is left for the reconcile to judge: a purchase keeps its cargo and its gold, and a sale loses the cargo without the gold. That is the state #12 closes, with nothing left to detect it. A crash of the server process alone, which is what the tests stop at, is not affected: the kernel already holds the rename.

**Fix.** In `save_char_checked()`, after `rename()`, open the file's directory and `fsync()` it, so the row is deleted only once the file that names it cannot be lost. A failure of that fsync should be logged and not returned: the new file is in place by then, and a FALSE would send the undo against a file that already holds the gold (the invariant the record states for a failed save). Every other caller of the checked save gets the same guarantee.

Fixed in `74ee6fe5d`, as you propose.

- After the `rename()`, `save_char_checked()` opens the player file's directory and `fsync()`s it (`save_char_sync_directory()`), so the settlement's row is deleted only once the file that names it would survive a crash of the host.
- A failure is logged and not returned, for the reason you give. The helper returns nothing, and its comment says why, so a later change cannot turn it into a FALSE by accident.
- Every caller of the checked save, and of `save_char()`, gets the same guarantee.

**Checked** with `strace` on a settlement test. Each save is now:

```text
openat("plrfiles/P-T/tern.plr.save-tmp.ymi1lD", O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0600) = 4
fsync(4)                                = 0
rename("plrfiles/P-T/tern.plr.save-tmp.ymi1lD", "plrfiles/P-T/tern.plr") = 0
openat("plrfiles/P-T", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) = 4
fsync(4)                                = 0
```

and the settlement's `DELETE` follows it. A power loss is not something a test here can produce, so there is no test of the durability itself; the coverage job runs 17 of the 19 changed lines of `players.c` (floor 61.37), and the two it does not run are the log of a failed sync and the return for a path without a directory.

`docs/systems/PLAYER_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM.md` and the settlement section of `VESSEL_SYSTEM.md` describe the save's rename and directory sync.

**Review of `vessels-s14-base..vessels-s14` (head `5293b0ac0`)**

Two findings, each in its own thread, both P3. Nothing above that.

1. A settlement is undone on whatever hull holds the fleet slot (`src/vessels/vessels_settlement.c:71`).
2. The row is deleted on a save that a host crash can still lose (`src/vessels/vessels_settlement.c:388`).

What I ran, in a scratch worktree at the head against a disposable MariaDB 10.11 built from `master_schema.sql`:

- The ten settlement tests pass. The whole suite: 2,028 run, 2 fail, both from my setup and neither in this MR (the pet legacy-migration test on a freshly created database, and the `lib/world` inventory test in a tree without `lib/world`).
- The pre-commit hooks on the changed files and `check_build_parity.py` pass.
- Probes of paths no test runs. All came out right, and they are worth keeping as tests:
  - `dockfees pay` with `mysql_test_drop_connection_at("COMMIT", 1, TRUE)`: paid once (975 gold, fee 0, no row). With `FALSE`: "ledger is unavailable", gold unchanged, fee still 25 in memory and in `ship_runtime_state`. With `TRUE` and the database away for the read-back: `settlement_unresolved` set, fee 25 in memory, 0 and one row in the database; the next `dockfees pay` undoes it and then pays the fee once; a third finds nothing owed.
  - `contractaccept` with the reply lost and the database away: "cannot record that freight", freight out of the hold, contract `1:Tern` with one row; the next `contractaccept` undoes it and accepts once (one bond, 10 units, no row).

Looked for and not found: cargo kept with its gold, a double sale, or a lost bond or fee from a single fault; a marker in memory that differs from the file outside `vessel_settlement_pay()`; a gated command that reads the hold or the fee before its gate; a second open row for a ship or a player; a table in the three transactions that is not InnoDB.

**Review round 1: both findings fixed** (range `vessels-s14..feat/vessels-s14`, head `b485062c8`)

1. A settlement undone on whatever hull holds the fleet slot: fixed in `bf82f7c93`. A slot whose rows are still stored is held, a spawn passes it by, and `shippurge` clears it. Details in the thread.
2. The row deleted on a save a host crash can still lose: fixed in `74ee6fe5d`. The save syncs the directory after the rename. Details in the thread.

Your four probes are kept as `Test_vessel_settlement_settles_a_fee_and_a_bond_without_a_reply` (`a5abda25b`): the dock-fee payment with the reply lost, with the `COMMIT` never arriving, and with the database away for the read-back (then the next payment and a third), and the freight acceptance with the reply lost and the database away (then the next acceptance). Each asserts the outcome you saw.

The two failures of your whole-suite run are not this MR's. The pet legacy-migration test fails on any database built from `master_schema.sql` alone when the syntax-check boot has not run against it first; I reproduced that at this head and recorded it as work item #18. The `lib/world` inventory test needs `lib/world`, which a scratch worktree does not have.

Verified on `63ee4c809`, the last commit that changes code:

| Check | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `make test-all`, database cases on | 2,030 production tests and 32 protocol tests pass |
| Live held-slot check, twice (private-namespace harness, dump reload) | boot held slot 13, `vedit spawn` took 14, `shippurge 13` freed it, the next spawn took 13 |
| Live gates | builder and economy pass |
| Local CI matrix (`--base gitlab/master`) | 33 of 33 jobs pass |

The record is in the Phase 14 section of `docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md` (`b485062c8`), and the description has a "Review round 1" section. Both threads are resolved; the merge request is mergeable and not merged. After the merge the help sync has one more entry (SHIPLIST, the SHIP-ADMIN entry).
